chunks: From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi, from Ismail ibn Abbad, who said, 'Bakr said, and I think I heard it from Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:'

'We love the one who is intellectual, understanding, scholarly, forbearing, kind, patient, truthful, and loyal. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has specialized the Prophets with the noble mannerisms. So whoever has them, let him praise Allah for that, and whoever does not have them, let him beseech Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him for them.'

He said, 'I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what are these?' He said: 'These are piety, contentment, patience, gratitude, forbearance, bashfulness, generosity, bravery, self-esteem, goodwill, truthfulness of speech, and fulfillment of trust.'
ai.seo_question: What are the noble character traits of the Prophets according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'makarim al-akhlaq' (noble character traits) as a divine gift specifically bestowed upon the Prophets, establishing them as the ideal model for Shia believers. He enumerates twelve key virtues, including piety, patience, and truthfulness, instructing followers to either thank Allah for possessing these traits or supplicate for their acquisition, thereby linking spiritual excellence directly to prophetic emulation.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Hashimy, from Ismail Bin Abbad who said, 
‘Bakr said, and I think he heard it from Ismail, from Abu Abdullah Bin Bakr, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> love the one who was an intellectual, understanding, scholarly, forbearing, kind, patient, truthful, loyal.

Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Specialise the Prophets<sup>as</sup> with the noble mannerisms. So the one in whom these are, so let him Praise Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon that, and the one in whom these do not happen to be, so let him beseech to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and let him ask Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what are these?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These are – the piety, and the contentment, and the patience, and the gratefulness, and the forbearance, and the bashfulness, and the generosity, and the bravery, and the self-esteem, and the goodwill, and truthful of the discussion, and payment of the entrustment’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him from Bakr ibn Salih from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Hashimi from Isma’il ‘Abbad who has said that perhaps he has heard it from Isma’il from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“We certainly love a person of reason, of good understanding, who has good knowledge and understanding of the law, who is forbearing, who is kind, who bears patience, who is truthful and who is loyal. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has chosen the prophets for noble moral (human) qualities. Whoever has them (noble qualities) should be thankful to Allah. Whoever does not have them he must pray humbly to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and request Him to grant them to him.

“I (the narrator) then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what are the noble qualities?’ “The Imam said, ‘They consist of restraint from indulging in worldly matters, to be content, to bear patience, to be thankful, to be forbearing, to be bashful, to be generous, to have dignity, to be virtuous, to be truthful in one’s words and to be trustworthy.’”
